With a mission to financially empower the next generation, Sezzle is revolutionizing the shopping experience beyond payments, blending cutting-edge tech with seamless, interest-free installment plans that make shopping smarter and more accessible.

We’re not just transforming payments; we’re redefining how people discover, interact with, and purchase the things they love while driving real impact on merchant sales through increased conversions and higher order values.

As we continue to shape the future of fintech and retail, we’re building an innovative, dynamic team passionate about creating more than just a transaction but a truly unique shopping journey.

If you’re excited about pushing boundaries in tech and delivering a game-changing experience for consumers and merchants alike, come join us at Sezzle and help create the future of shopping! About the Role:

We are seeking a talented and motivated Fraud Operations Analyst who is best in class with a high IQ plus a high EQ. This role presents an exciting opportunity to thrive in a dynamic, fast-paced environment within a rapidly growing team, with abundant prospects for career advancement.

As part of optimizing the online shopping experience, Sezzle constantly monitors users and transactions for abusive or fraudulent behavior. Our Fraud Operations team reviews suspicious activity flagged by Sezzle ’s fraud detection system or escalated from Customer Support agents.

Fraud Operations Analysts will block users deemed fraudulent or risky, and clear false positive flags from our automated systems and support agents. We monitor for new trends in fraudulent behavior and continuously evolve our policies and procedures to stay one step ahead.

We are looking for a teammate who can work one of the shifts listed below full-time: Sunday – Thursday, 8:00 am – 4:30 pm - Central Time. This will be a non-exempt/hourly position. Due to the requirements of the position, only English resumes will be accepted.

For this Fraud Operations Analyst the compensation range is $1,500 - $2,000 USD GROSS per month as a contractor. This range is designed to reflect the skills, experience, and value brought to the team, ensuring competitive and fair pay within the industry. What You'll Do:
Monitor real-time transactions and other customer behaviors flagged for fraud and abuse for manual review.
Investigate individual transactions using internal policies and review methodologies to determine if the transactions are fraudulent or not.
Understand our systems and tools; investigate account patterns through data analysis.
Research fraud and user behavior to contribute to machine learning models, rules and other detection systems.
Collaborate with analysts, operations specialists, data scientists and engineering to improve our fraud prevention mechanisms, processes and tools.
Learn and maintain strong domain knowledge of the world of fraud including prevention techniques and technologies.
Maintain or exceed established service level agreements (SLAs) for timely resolution of queued cases to minimize potential losses.
Handle escalations from internal and external stakeholders in a professional and efficient manner.

Bachelor's degree from an accredited institution
Minimum 1 year of experience in investigating and resolving fraud incidents
Experienced in analyzing data and comfortable making impactful decisions in a fast-paced and sometimes ambiguous environment
Attention to detail and ability to multitask
Excellent problem-solving and analytical skills
Strong business judgment and communication skills
Ability to self-start and work with minimal supervision after training
Able to work through holidays
Demonstrated experience working with Claude or equivalent large language model tools is required; candidates must be comfortable leveraging AI to enhance productivity, research, and communication.

Work experience in fintech, payments, lending, banking, or financial institutions is a plus
Degree in statistics, math, finance, economics, or related quantitative discipline; graduate degree a plus
Experience in using database query language (e.g. SQL, etc), and data processing and analytics tools such as Python / R / SAS is a plus
Ideal candidate will be available to start within two weeks following an offer

You need action - speed matters in business. Many decisions and actions are reversible and do not need extensive study. We value calculated risk-taking.

You earn trust - you listen attentively, speak candidly, and treat others respectfully.

You have backbone; disagree, then commit - you can respectfully challenge decisions when you disagree, even when doing so is uncomfortable or exhausting. You have conviction and are tenacious. You do not compromise for the sake of social cohesion. Once a decision is determined, you commit wholly.

You deliver results - you focus on the key inputs and deliver them with the right quality and in a timely fashion. Despite setbacks, you rise to the occasion and never settle.

McKesson is currently seeking an Operations Manager in our Mason, OH office. The Operations Manager is responsible for the operational activities of a variety of functional departments, distribution center(s), or facility(ies). Reviews and analyzes reports, records, and directives, and confers with managers/ supervisors to obtain data required for planning activities, such as new commitments, status of work in progress, and problems encountered.

Roles & Responsibilities: May be responsible for one or more of the following activities related to the receiving, storing, and/ or shipping of materials or finished goods.

May be responsible for ensuring materials are received from proper vendors, delivered to inventory, and finished goods, are available to meet production schedules, packaged according to specification and shipped in a timely manner. Ensures the security and accountability of materials and goods with inventory control.

May evaluate current procedures and practices for accomplishing department objectives and develop and implement improved procedures and practices. Gives work direction, resolves problems, and sets deadlines to ensure timely completion of work. Monitors and analyzes costs and prepares budgets.

Employee Management Ensures high quality employee attraction, engagement, and development at all levels. Builds bench strength through modeling ICARE/ILEAD and development of a high-performing culture. Work with regional management on succession planning.

Effectively manage all people issues including, but not limited to, labor, turnover, generational, and diversity and inclusion. Provides leadership and support for on-going training initiatives for management and employees. Develop a strong team of DC leaders and provide coaching and appropriate development opportunities for direct reports.

Directs staff to provide a work environment that fosters creativity, productivity, collaboration, and accountability. Maintains an engaged work environment by having a strong and friendly presence both on the floor and in the office.

Acts as an advocate for the facility’s management team to ensure swift resolution to both software and hardware problems. General Management and Operations Collaborates with both regional management and local management to develop and align strategic initiatives to implement locally.

Actively oversees DC operations and management by giving work direction, resolving problems, setting deadlines to ensure timely completion of work. Develops the vision for the facility, while tracking current processes and regularly assessing if best practices are in place.

Collaborates with colleagues in other 3PL operations to drive consistency or processes and the development of the RxCrossroads by McKesson 3PL brand. Financial Ownership Utilizes financial acumen and knowledge, especially in making business decisions. Monitors and analyze costs and assist the management team in making budget.

Directs local operations to ensure building’s performance is within budget and expense plans. Cross-Function Partnerships Collaborates with stakeholders from HR, Engineering, Six Sigma, Finance, and more to ensure operations are identifying, meeting, and exceeding desired output and best practices.

Coordinates with Transportation team and Contractors. Strategizes with leaders across the network to stay ahead of changing customer needs, industry advances, and labor planning concerns. Facilitates success within the building by monitoring, preventing and solving any concerns outside of the distribution center.

Compliance and Safety Oversee compliance with federal, state, local, and company policies and safety regulations. Assist the management team in diagnosing any safety concerns and creating ideal solutions. Ensure the building is always prepared for either an internal or external audit.

Minimum Job Qualifications (Knowledge, Skills, & Abilities): Degree or equivalent experience. Typically requires 6+ years of relevant professional experience and 0-2 years of supervisory experience. Critical Skills Capable of handling multiple priorities and extensive time demands regarding both logistics and employee problems and engagement.

Effectively navigates through complex situations, both internal and external, that may require multiple decision makers. Advanced knowledge of Operations/Distribution/Pharma Supply Chain Management. Excellent organizational skills, excellent communication skills (verbal/written), management skills, and contract negotiations.

Advanced financial and business acumen to include knowledge of key financial statements drivers and levers. Ability to develop, drive, implement and maintain innovation and promote continuous improvement around engineering processes, customer support, cost structure and quality initiatives. Experience with DEA regulation compliance.

Florida Designated Representative licensed. Additional Skills Strong PC skills and the ability to use McKesson’s suite of PC-based applications (Excel, Word, PowerPoint, Microsoft, Outlook, etc.). Experience with warehouse management systems. Six Sigma training or continuous improvement experience.

SAP experience is a plus Working Conditions: Multiple environments including office and warehouse. Must be willing to work various hours to manage across the 24-hour work day within the distribution center.

At OpenAI, our Trust, Safety & Risk Operations teams safeguard our products, users, and the company from abuse, fraud, scams, regulatory non-compliance, and other emerging risks. We operate at the intersection of operations, compliance, user trust, and safety working closely with Legal, Policy, Engineering, Product, Go-To-Market, and external partners to ensure our platforms are safe, compliant, and trusted by a diverse, global user base.
The Global Safety Response Operations team within the org provides 24/7 coverage for user safety, risk, and regulatory escalations across OpenAI’s products, handling the highest-priority cases that require human judgment and rapid response. The team operates as the core escalations management and delivery arm of OpenAI’s safety operations, ensuring that our products remain safe and aligned with our policies while enabling timely, empathetic, and consistent user support.
We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.
Please note: This role may involve exposure to sensitive content, including material that is sexual, violent, or otherwise disturbing.

We’re looking for experienced Trust, Safety, and Risk Operations analysts who have subject matter expertise in one or more of the following areas: policy enforcement and content moderation, fraud and scam prevention, developer risk, or privacy and regulatory escalations.

You’ll be on the front lines of safety escalation management, helping to triage and resolve urgent and sensitive cases. You’ll work across subject matter areas, systems, and processes to ensure operational excellence, develop process improvements and automations, and surface insights and trends.

The Bike Club, we're on a mission to make sustainable, high-quality cycling accessible to every family. Our subscription model lets kids always ride the right-sized bike — and when they grow, we swap it out, refurbish it, and pass it on. With 80,000+ bikes on the road, $50M+ in funding, and rapid expansion across Europe, we're just getting started.
We're looking for a Lean Operations Manager to drive continuous improvement across our warehouse, refurbishment, and fulfilment operations in Rainham, London. This is a hands-on, gemba-first role for someone who thrives on the warehouse floor, loves solving operational puzzles, and turns observation and data into measurable change.
We've intentionally designed this as a single, broad role with real scope — and we're open to candidates at very different career stages. If you're early in your career but ambitious, structured, and hungry to step up, this is a rare chance to grow into a senior-style operations. If you're more experienced, you'll find plenty of room to take ownership from day one.
You'll partner closely with our warehouse leads, mechanics, customer service, and last-mile partners to remove waste, increase throughput, and make every refurbished bike move faster and more reliably from intake to family. Your work will directly shape how we scale a circular operation across Europe.
Tasks
Drive the continuous improvement roadmap across intake, refurbishment, dispatch, and returns — set priorities, run the program, and report progress to leadership
Map value streams end-to-end (bike intake → refurb → QC → outbound → courier → customer → return) and identify the bottlenecks, waste, and rework slowing us down
Run kaizen workshops, A3 problem-solving sessions, and structured root-cause analyses with mechanics, warehouse operators, and team leads
Define, track, and improve operational KPIs (cycle time, refurb throughput, first-time-right rate, on-time dispatch, returns turnaround, OEE on key stations)
Roll out standard work, 5S, visual management, and pull-based flow across the warehouse and refurb workshop
Spend significant time on the floor — observing, coaching, and validating that improvements stick after rollout
Lead capacity and layout planning as we scale: workstation design, station balancing, tool placement, and bike flow
Partner with last-mile and courier providers to reduce failed deliveries, returns leakage, and customer waiting time
Build the data and reporting backbone we need to manage operations by fact (Excel, WMS, Salesforce, BI tools)
Coach team leads and operators in lean thinking, building improvement capability across the organisation

A genuine gemba mindset — you'd rather be on the warehouse floor than behind a desk
Structured, analytical problem-solving — you can break a messy operational problem down and use data (Excel at minimum) to point at the answer
Strong communication and collaboration skills — comfortable working with mechanics and operators just as easily as with senior stakeholders
Pragmatic, organised, and biased to action — you thrive in a fast-moving scale-up where things change weekly
A relevant degree (industrial engineering, logistics, supply chain, business engineering, or similar)
Some real exposure to operations — through internships, working student roles, a first full-time job, a thesis project, or a few years of hands-on experience
Real curiosity about lean / continuous improvement — bonus points for a Lean Six Sigma certification (Yellow, Green, or Black Belt) or demonstrated kaizen / value stream experience
Confidence with operational systems (WMS, ERP, Salesforce, ticketing tools); SQL or BI tooling is a plus, not a requirement
Fluent English (working language); German is a strong plus
Bonus: interest or experience in circular economy, refurbishment, subscription business models, or sustainable mobility

Holidays – 25 days annual leave plus bank holidays
Private medical insurance

Parental leave – enhanced maternity and paternity leave
Bike subscription – £30 on Bike Club subscriptions
Sustainability impact – you will be working for a B Corp Certified company that actively contributes to environmental and social good
If you're earlier in your career and not sure you tick every box: please apply anyway. Drive, structure, and a willingness to learn matter more to us than years on a CV.

The Opportunity
Okta is building an AI-enabled demand engine that uses signals, automation, and intelligent engagement to identify, qualify, route, and progress the right buyers more effectively. The AI Journey Operations Manager will own the business strategy, qualification framework, routing logic, operating model, and performance optimization for AI-assisted xDR capabilities across the Global Demand Center.
This role is not primarily a platform administration or workflow-build role. It is a senior, cross-functional capability-owner role responsible for determining how AI-assisted qualification and engagement should operate, how it connects to human xDR and Sales follow-up, and how it contributes to measurable funnel and pipeline outcomes.
The ideal candidate combines AI-enabled GTM experience, xDR/Sales process knowledge, demand generation, revenue operations, and journey strategy. They can translate business priorities into qualification logic, routing rules, AI engagement workflows, handoff requirements, measurement frameworks, and ongoing optimization plans.

Define qualification frameworks for AI-assisted engagement across priority inbound, account-based, product-led, customer, and signal-triggered motions.
Establish the fit, behavior, intent, engagement, and business-context criteria used to determine whether a lead or account should be engaged, progressed, routed, recycled, or suppressed.
Partner with Revenue Operations, xDR leadership, Sales Operations, and Marketing to align AI qualification logic with lifecycle definitions and Sales acceptance requirements.
Establish governance for qualification-model changes, exceptions, and regional or segment-specific variations.
Design routing, handoff, and disposition models
Define AI qualification criteria based on fit, intent, behavior, engagement, account context, and business priority. Partner with Sales, xDR, Revenue Operations, Marketing Operations, Growth, and Journey teams to determine when AI should engage, when a human xDR or seller should take over, and when an account should move into nurture, suppression, or another follow-up path.
Design next-best-action rules, handoff thresholds, escalation paths, service-level expectations, and exception handling.
Establish consistent acceptance, rejection, disposition, recycling, and re-entry processes across Marketing, AI xDR, and Sales teams.
Identify and resolve leakage, latency, and ownership gaps between AI engagement and human follow-up.
Connect AI xDR to revenue outcomes
Define how AI xDR performance will be measured across qualified engagement, human acceptance, meetings, opportunity creation, pipeline progression, and other agreed funnel outcomes.
Partner with Revenue Operations and Analytics to establish reporting, attribution, and feedback loops.
Diagnose where AI-engaged leads and accounts stall or fail to progress and recommend changes to qualification, routing, handoff, or follow-up logic.
Use funnel data to prioritize use cases and determine where AI xDR should expand, change, or stop.
Lead the cross-functional operating model
Serve as the primary business owner for AI xDR across Marketing, xDR, Sales, Revenue Operations, Sales Operations, and Journey Architecture.
Translate business policies and revenue-process requirements into specifications for technical builders and platform administrators.
Establish decision rights, governance, documentation, testing, launch readiness, and ongoing change-management processes.
Lead expansion planning across regions, segments, platforms, and use cases.
Guide workflow implementation
Partner with Qualified, Outreach, CRM, marketing automation, and related platform owners to ensure workflows reflect approved qualification, routing, and handoff requirements.
Validate that implementation matches the intended business logic and revenue operating model.
Monitor workflow accuracy, operational compliance, and downstream outcomes.
Recommend technical or process changes based on funnel performance and stakeholder feedback.

7+ years of experience in B2B demand generation, revenue operations, Sales operations, xDR operations, marketing operations, growth operations, or a related GTM operations discipline.
Experience with AI SDR or AI xDR platforms, conversational marketing, automated qualification, or agent-assisted engagement.
Demonstrated experience designing or operationalizing AI-assisted, automated, or rules-based qualification and engagement workflows in a B2B GTM environment. Strong understanding of how Marketing, xDR, and Sales processes connect to opportunity creation and pipeline progression.
Experience defining business rules and translating them into technical workflow requirements.
Experience partnering directly with xDR leadership, Sales Operations, Revenue Operations, and Sales stakeholders.
Strong analytical ability, including experience evaluating conversion, acceptance, progression, and pipeline performance.
Ability to lead a complex cross-functional capability without direct authority.
Strong documentation, governance, and operating-process design skills.
Familiarity with Qualified, Outreach, Salesforce, Marketo, Common Room, Clay, or comparable GTM platforms.

Experience designing routing models, next-best-action frameworks, or automated Sales handoffs.
Experience supporting enterprise B2B SaaS go-to-market motions.
Experience in cybersecurity, identity, developer platforms, customer identity, application development, or cloud infrastructure.
Experience marketing to Product, Engineering, developer, application, or technical buyer audiences.
Experience with account-based, product-led, signal-led, customer expansion, and partner-influenced demand motions.
Experience in lead or account qualification, lifecycle management, routing, disposition, recycling, and Sales handoff processes.

Human xDR and Sales acceptance rates.
Speed and quality of AI-to-human handoffs.
Reduction in routing, ownership, and follow-up leakage.
Progression from AI engagement to meetings, opportunities, and pipeline.
Adoption and confidence among xDR, Sales, Marketing, and Revenue Operations stakeholders.
Scalability and governance of the AI xDR operating model.

At Vanta, our mission is to help businesses earn and prove trust. We believe that security should be monitored and verified continuously, and we empower companies to practice better security and prove it with ease. Vanta has a kind and talented team, and while some have prior security experience, many have been successful at Vanta without it.
You will own the data Vanta's EPD organization actually runs on — bringing new signal sources online, standardizing them at the point of ingestion, and building the systems that make the underlying data trustworthy rather than merely stored.
The EPD Systems team is building the infrastructure Vanta's engineering, product, and design organization depends on to understand itself. Not by asking teams to be more diligent but by going to the source, processing it, standardizing it, and pushing value back out so each source of truth earns its own adoption.

s.h: What you’ll do as a Operations Manager, Signal Systems at Vanta
s.t:
Bring new signal sources online end to end — from discovery and scoping through ingestion, standardization, and live operation
Identify the specific failure modes in each information source and build systems that mitigate them at the point of ingestion
Go to the teams that produce and consume a signal, understand what the information actually means and what they need back from it, and build accordingly
Replace human-diligence dependencies with engineering solutions: derive fields, pull from source systems, validate at write time
Build alongside teammates who are growing into building — raise their technical ceiling, not just your own output
Partner with the inference and systems layers to ensure what you produce is queryable, trustworthy, and ready to build on

s.h: How to be successful in this role
s.t:
You look at a data source and see its failure modes before its contents: where it lies, where it goes stale, where it's duplicated, where the schema won't hold at 10x
Your first move on an adherence problem is an engineering answer — derive it, pull it, or validate it at write time. Better forms and nudges are your last resort
You've shipped something yourself in roughly the last 12–18 months — a pipeline, an internal tool, a working prototype, an agent — and you can walk through the code and defend your choices. Specs handed to an engineer don't count for this bar
You've built something real with Claude, an LLM API, or agentic tooling — not "I use ChatGPT for drafts." You'll be asked what broke and how you worked around it
You build alongside people: some teammates do program-delivery work today and should grow into building; you see growing their capability as part of your mandate, not a tax on it
You go find out what the data means by talking to the people who produce and consume it, and you come back with a changed understanding — not a requirements list
We use AI to augment our own capabilities and invest deeply in helping every Vantan enhance their work through AI
No CS degree or formal engineering tenure required. Shipping real things fast with AI-assisted tooling clears our bar
Open to using AI to amplify their skills and strengthen their work - demonstrating curiosity, a willingness to learn, and sound judgment in applying AI responsibly to improve efficiency and impact.

In dieser Schlüsselposition übernimmst du die operative Führung unserer Betriebe mit Hauptfokus auf Kaiseraugst. Du berichtest direkt an den Geschäftsführer und führst rund 15–20 Mitarbeitende. Du führst nicht vom Büro aus, sondern bist dort präsent, wo der Betrieb läuft. Wenn du Teams mit Respekt und klarer Kante führst und Technik verstehst, bist du bei uns am richtigen Platz.

s.h: Deine Aufgaben – führen, organisieren und weiterentwickeln
s.t:
Betrieb führen: Du führst das operative Tagesgeschäft unserer Standorte mit Hauptfokus Kaiseraugst. Du planst den täglichen Mitarbeiter\- und Maschineneinsatz, setzt Prioritäten und sorgst dafür, dass der Betrieb reibungslos läuft.
Team führen: Du leitest rund 15–20 Mitarbeitende (Platzchef, Maschinisten, Sortier\-/Betriebspersonal, Waage) mit klarer, fairer und verlässlicher Kommunikation auf Augenhöhe.
Materialflüsse koordinieren: Du behältst den Überblick über Annahme, Klassierung, Sortierung, Lagerung und Abtransport unserer Wertstoffe und Abfälle und stellst sicher, dass Materialien zur richtigen Zeit am richtigen Ort sind.
Betrieb weiterentwickeln: Du erkennst Verbesserungspotenziale in Abläufen, Organisation und Technik und setzt diese gemeinsam mit der Geschäftsführung pragmatisch um.
Maschinenpark im Schuss halten: Du sorgst dafür, dass unsere Bagger, Radlader, Stapler, Pressen, Schredder sowie Aufbereitungs\- und Sortieranlagen einsatzbereit, gewartet und gepflegt sind. Grössere Reparaturen sprichst du mit externen Partnern ab.
Platz \& Sicherheit: Du schaust auf Sauberkeit, Struktur und Ordnung auf dem gesamten Areal und setzt Sicherheits\-, Umwelt\- und Brandschutzregeln konsequent durch.
Verantwortung übernehmen: Du vertrittst den Geschäftsführer bei Abwesenheit und bringst deine Ideen bei Neuanschaffungen und Projekten ein.
Das bringst du mit – Führung, Technik und gesunder Menschenverstand:
Berufsausbildung: Abgeschlossene technische, handwerkliche oder vergleichbare Berufsausbildung.
Weiterbildung: Eine Weiterbildung zum Technischen , Prozessfachmann, Betriebsfachmann oder eine vergleichbare Qualifikation ist von Vorteil.
Führungserfahrung: Führungserfahrung in einem operativen Umfeld mit unterschiedlich qualifizierten Mitarbeitenden ist besonders willkommen. Du kommunizierst direkt, respektvoll, klar und lässt dich auch in hektischen Momenten nicht aus der Ruhe bringen.
Hands\-on\-Mentalität: Du packst Probleme pragmatisch an, entscheidest und organisierst gerne und bist im Betrieb sichtbar und präsent.
Wohnort: Dein Wohnort ermöglicht dir eine zuverlässige Präsenz in Kaiseraugst.
Führerschein: Führerausweis Kat. B ist Pflicht; Baumaschinenausweis und/oder Maschinistenpraxis sind ein Plus.
Branchenerfahrung: Erfahrung im Recycling\-, Schüttgut\- oder Baustellenbereich ist von Vorteil – motivierte Quereinsteiger mit solider Führungspraxis sind willkommen!

Viel Freiraum: Hohe Eigenverantwortung und echtes Vertrauen in deine tägliche Arbeit.
Schlüsselposition: Du arbeitest direkt mit dem Geschäftsführer zusammen und kannst den Betrieb aktiv mitgestalten.
Abwechslungsreicher Betrieb: Unterschiedliche Materialien, Maschinen, Anlagen und Standorte sorgen dafür, dass kein Tag genau gleich aussieht.
Sicherer Arbeitsplatz: Ein wirtschaftlich gesundes, regional verankertes KMU mit kurzen Entscheidungswegen und langjährigen Mitarbeitenden.
Moderne Technik: Gute Maschinen und zeitgemässe Recyclinganlagen.
Klare Verantwortlichkeiten: Administration, ISO\-System, Budgetierung und Fuhrparkmanagement werden durch andere Stellen unterstützt bzw. verantwortet – du kannst dich auf die operative Führung der Betriebe konzentrieren.
Zeitgemässe Anstellungsbedingungen: 5 Wochen Ferien, gute Sozialleistungen und faire, marktgerechte Anstellungsbedingungen.
Bereit für den nächsten Schritt?
Sende uns deine Bewerbung bitte direkt. Deine Bewerbung behandeln wir selbstverständlich vertraulich. Auf die Bewerbungsadresse hat ausschliesslich der Geschäftsführer Zugriff.
(Hinweis: Wir berücksichtigen ausschliesslich Direktbewerbungen. Dossiers von Personalvermittlern können wir nicht bearbeiten.)

Because this is a new category of devices, you’ll have the opportunity to build the lab operating model early—shaping the systems, standards, and workflows that support products from prototype through launch.

Own device fleet and inventory: Manage configuration, deployment, tracking, lifecycle, and accurate asset records for a large fleet of consumer devices and test equipment; coordinate receiving, storage, checkout, shipping, transfers, spares, and secure disposal .
Operate and maintain the lab: Keep racks, benches, test rigs, cabling, power, networking, peripherals, and shared equipment reliable and organized; diagnose issues and coordinate repairs, replacements, and preventive maintenance .

Support testing and diagnostics: Partner with engineering and QA on large-scale test automation setups, failure reproduction, diagnostics collection, log capture, and environment resets .
Plan lab readiness and capacity: Track fleet health, rig availability, utilization, and upcoming test needs; identify constraints before they block testing .
Partner across teams: Work with hardware, systems, QA, reliability, IT, and infrastructure teams to keep the lab ready for development and release activities .

Proven track-record of operating or supporting a hardware, electronics, reliability, manufacturing, or QA test lab.
Hands-on experience managing fleets of consumer electronics, embedded devices, prototypes, or connected hardware.
Comfortable setting up, configuring, troubleshooting, and maintaining devices, test rigs, networking, power systems, and peripherals across USB, Wi-Fi, Ethernet, Bluetooth, power, and device connectivity.

Enjoy improving the reliability, scalability, and efficiency of physical lab operations.

Sales Operations Analyst
Reports to: Sales Operations Manager
Job purpose: Support the administration, calculation, and reconciliation of sales compensation across a fast-growing global SaaS sales organization. Own the monthly mechanics that keep sellers paid accurately and on time, while helping build new processes, including bookings reconciliation and contract automation, as the team and the business scale.
Employment type: Permanent, full-time.
Locations: Must be based in the Atlanta, GA area. This is a hybrid role, with occasional in-person meetings in the Atlanta office.

What We Do
RELEX runs the planning decisions behind 600+ retailers and manufacturers worldwide, deciding, at real scale, what gets forecast, stocked, priced, promoted, and produced across the entire value chain.

Few problems combine this much data, this much complexity, and this much real-world weight: get it right and a shelf stays stocked, a factory line doesn’t stall, food doesn’t spoil in a warehouse before it’s sold. Get it wrong, and it shows up in actual losses, for some of the largest retail and manufacturing brands in the world.
We’ve grown for 76 consecutive quarters straight, and it’s still accelerating. The first half of 2026 was the strongest in the company’s history. We’re a team of 2,000+ people, headquartered in Helsinki, with offices across Europe, North America, and Asia-Pacific.
In response to our fast growth and market expansion, we are looking for ...
What we need you to do and be
Calculate monthly sales commissions, process manual adjustments, and maintain accurate crediting records across the sales organization.
Conduct crediting reviews and periodic audits, catching and resolving discrepancies before they reach the field.
Coordinate with Payroll to ensure commission payments are processed accurately and on schedule each cycle.
Investigate and resolve compensation disputes raised by sellers and managers, escalating complex cases where needed.
Administer and maintain our sales compensation platform, keeping calculations, adjustments, and records current and reliable. This includes improving the platform's UI and the seller experience so sellers see only what's relevant to their own commissions, driving transparency and adoption across the field.
Lead the rollout of a contracts platform into the deal-closing motion, including configuration and automation that connects signed contracts to the compensation and booking process.
Design and formalize a bookings review and reconciliation process, partnering with Finance to validate the bookable figures that drive seller payouts.
Serve as a first line of support for sellers, fielding and resolving questions on payments, timing, and crediting.
Document new processes as they take shape, building a clear reference for the team as compensation administration scales with the business.

s.h: What you’ll bring to the table
s.t:
Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Business, Operations, Accounting, Economics, or a related field.
Curious and eager to learn, with a general understanding of how sales operations functions within a global SaaS organization.
A self-starter with a willingness to get things done.
Strong attention to detail and comfort working with numbers, spreadsheets, and calculations under recurring monthly deadlines, while supporting individuals across multiple timezones.
Analytical mindset, able to spot discrepancies, investigate root causes, and communicate findings clearly.
Comfortable operating with some ambiguity; several of this role's responsibilities are new to the team and will take shape as you help build them.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain compensation outcomes clearly to sellers and managers.
Able to triage and prioritize recurring monthly deadlines alongside longer-term projects.

Experience in sales operations, sales compensation, finance, or a related operational role is a plus, but not required. We are open to candidates with little to no professional experience who demonstrate a strong interest in B2B SaaS or enterprise software and a desire to build a career in sales operations.

Excel skills (pivot tables, lookups, basic modeling).
This role supports a global sales organization, so fluency in languages beyond English is a plus.

You’ll be supported and given the space to thrive. We offer meaningful work, flexibility, and a culture that backs you to share your voice and be authentic.

Du kommunizierst verbindlich, priorisierst klar und bleibst handlungsfähig, wenn Anforderungen unvollständig sind oder kurz vor einem Termin ein Problem auftaucht.

Echte Verantwortung: Du führst eigene Projekte und hast direkten Einfluss auf Kunden, Abläufe und Produktqualität.

LOCATION: Remote, US (Candidates based in Los Angeles, CA highly preferred but if located elsewhere, we would require travel to the LA office one week a month)

Sunbit builds financial technology for real life. Our AI-native platform helps more people get to “yes” at the moments that matter with personalized offers, transparent terms, and no added consumer fees. In stores, practices and service centers across the country, Sunbit provides a fast, fair pay-over-time option. For everything else, the Sunbit Credit Card delivers a modern, no-fee credit experience managed in a powerful mobile app.
We are guided by people-centered values: Serve Others Before Self, Include Always, Connect Genuinely, Innovate for Good. These values shape how we build, how we support customers and merchants, and how we work with each other.
What makes Sunbit different is an AI-native infrastructure that runs through the full customer and merchant journey. Our interconnected AI systems power instant decisioning, streamline fraud checks with human-in-the-loop safeguards, and enable highly personalized offers at scale. The result is a quick, fair, and simple experience for consumers and merchants.
We pair this technology with inclusion and transparency. Sunbit delivers industry-leading approval rates — 90%+ in auto service and 85%+ in dental — while maintaining zero consumer fee-based revenue. It is a better way to serve people and merchants, proven at scale.
Today, Sunbit is available across nationwide, in-person merchant network of 30,000+ locations spanning auto service centers, dental and optical practices, veterinary clinics, and other specialty services. We help teams say “yes” more often and help customers move forward with confidence.

As a Strategy & Operations Manager at Sunbit , you will serve as the connective tissue between our executive vision and departmental execution.

You won’t just be building decks; you will be owning the lifecycle of critical initiatives—from diagnosing complex business problems to implementing digital product flows that impact growth, revenue, operations, and customer experience.

This role is designed for a high-performer who thrives in the intersection of data, product, and cross-functional leadership.

Strategic Planning: Lead high-priority initiatives that define the future of Sunbit ’s product offerings and market positioning.
Cross-Functional Leadership: Partner closely with Product, Engineering, Marketing, Operations, Legal, and Finance to ensure seamless execution of the company roadmap.
Product & Digital Optimization: Collaborate with the Product team to understand customer and merchant experience, identify areas for improvement, and refine digital flows and platform experiences, ensuring our technical solutions align with business KPIs.
Operational Excellence: Build and scale the "operating system" of your department—identifying bottlenecks in current processes and implementing scalable solutions.
Data-Driven Insights: Utilize advanced financial modeling and data analytics to track performance, forecast trends, and provide actionable recommendations to leadership.
Project Management: Drive cross-functional projects from planning to implementation, ensuring they stay on schedule, within scope, and deliver measurable impact.

Bachelor’s degree in business administration, Operations Management, Economics or a related field; an MBA is a plus.
10+ years of Strategy and Operations experience with 2+ years at the Manager or Senior Manager level.
The ideal candidate would have a mix of product management, project management, and analytics experience with significant cross-functional stakeholder alignment.
A background in Top-Tier Management Consulting (MBB, Big Four) and/or an in-house S&O role within a high-growth Tech, Financial Services, Fintech environment (lending, payments, consumer finance, etc.)
Experience working alongside Product teams and solid understanding of digital platforms, customer journeys, workflows, and operational systems.
Expert-level proficiency in financial modeling and data analytics; you are comfortable navigating large datasets to find the "so what."
Proven experience owning and implementing initiatives to execute on strategies.

Sunbit is recognized as one of the fastest-growing and most admired fintech companies, earning honors from Inc. 5000 (four consecutive years), Forbes Fintech 50, Deloitte Technology Fast 500, Financial Times, and FinTech Breakthrough for its innovation and impact. The company has also been featured among Newsweek’s Most Loved Workplaces and CB Insights’ Unicorn Companies, reflecting a valuation of $1.1B.
People choose Sunbit for its people-first culture rooted in service, inclusion, and real-world impact. About Halter
At Halter, we’re on a mission to enable farmers and graziers to run the most productive and sustainable operations. Our customers are using Halter to break free from the time-intensive constraints of conventional practices. Imagine watching 500 cattle stand up and walk calmly towards their next break? No quad bikes, no dogs, no fences.

Just a group of cattle walking at their own pace. People say it looks like magic. Our customers are revolutionizing grazing with Halter. It's changing lives and transforming an industry. People join Halter to do meaningful work. By joining us you’ll be solving challenging problems within a talented team and a culture built for high performance.

Our team out-think, out-work and out-care. We’re committed to delivering real change in the world - this isn’t easy, and in truth, we love that it’s hard.
We’re backed to deliver on a mission that matters by Tier 1 investors including Founders Fund , Bessemer Venture Partners , BOND, DCVC , Blackbird , Promus Ventures , Rocket Lab’s Peter Beck and Icehouse ventures .
To find out more, visit our LinkedIn & Instagram .

We're building Halter in Argentina/Uruguay from the ground up, while still deeply connected to our global offices and ways of working. Sales teams will be remote across both Argentina and Uruguay, and our other teams will be in the Buenos Aires office. And we’re a fast growing team.
You'll bring the vibes and be our boots on the ground for the day-to-day people operations that keep our Argentina and Uruguay teams running. Reporting to our Senior People & Performance Partner in Boulder, CO (US), you'll own the logistics, systems and cultural moments that hold a growing team together: IT and onboarding, the office, our local vehicle fleet, and the team moments people actually remember.
You won't be doing it alone. You'll partner closely with our People Operations & Programs team in New Zealand, fleet, people systems, compliance and health & safety, onboarding programs, and you'll be the local expert they depend on for anything Argentina/Uruguay.
We're creating this role because we're growing fast in a brand-new market, and this work can't wait. When a laptop doesn't get signed for or a vehicle handover slips, someone's first week is worse for it. You'll be the person who makes sure that doesn't happen.
This is a hands-on, varied role for someone early in their career or making a career pivot. We don't care whether you've done people operations before. We care that you excel at whatever you put your mind to, that might have looked like your studies, your sport, or something you built on your own time.

s.h: What Your Day Will Look Like
s.t:
You're in early because it's a new starter's first day. Their desk is ready, their laptop is provisioned, their merch is sorted. You want to be the one who meets them at the door.
It's 9:40 and a vehicle handover has gone sideways, the depot window moved. You drop what you're doing and sort it, because a Territory Manager without a truck can't work.
You're partnering with the Global Vehicle Fleet lead in New Zealand, working on building a more scalable process.
You overhear the customer team saying they haven't had a proper team moment in weeks. You make a note and do something about it on Friday.
Executives are flying in from Auckland and Boulder next month for a fortnight. You make the whole visit feel effortless.
You hit something nobody has written a process for. You solve it, then write the process, for Argentina first, then Uruguay.
You spend a day out on farm with a Territory Manager, because you can't support work you've never seen.
In short: operational people threads, fleet, office, and creating genuinely good experiences for our Argentina and Uruguay teams. You'll be the ask-me-anything for everyone here.

Someone who fills other people's cups. Introvert or extrovert genuinely doesn't matter to us — some of the best people on our team are each. What matters is that you give energy rather than take it, and that people want to follow you whatever your title says.
A mindset of unreasonable hospitality. You bring a customer-service instinct to how you treat colleagues.
Comfortable being uncomfortable. You'll do the job nobody wants to do because you can see it needs doing. High humility, no ego about the task.
Strong operationally, with proven ability to execute in fast-moving, ambiguous environments. Timing matters here — most of this work can't wait a week.
A systems thinker. You'll get fluent in our people systems fast and become the local expert others come to. You like building the process, not just working the queue.
High awareness and empathy. You read between the lines and put yourself in other people's shoes.
Excellent judgment and discretion. Thoughtful, high-integrity, trustworthy. People will tell you difficult things and you'll know what to do with them.
You don't need a People background. Our team has come from hospitality, retail, services, agency and design. Delivery and curiosity beat a linear HR CV.
You've grown wherever you've been — promoted, trusted with more, handed the hard thing. Or you've followed what you find genuinely interesting rather than climbing a ladder. Both are good signals to us.
Hungry and ambitious , with the horsepower to grow as the business does.
Fluent in Spanish and English. You'll be the bridge between the Argentine team and colleagues in New Zealand and the US.
Based in Buenos Aires and up for five days a week with the team. Our space is in Vicente López to start.
Genuinely interested in the work — land, livestock, and the people who farm it.
Where this could go
We're not hiring a coordinator forever. We're hiring the person who builds the foundation in Argentina, then helps us do it again in Uruguay and beyond. If you're good, this is one of the best seats in the company to grow from.
What this role isn't
Some of this work is physical, urgent and unglamorous. You'll sign for deliveries and stand in queues. Processes will break and you'll be the one who notices. There's no playbook yet, and for a while you'll be writing it while doing the job. If that sounds frustrating rather than exciting, this isn't the right role — and that's genuinely fine.
Our Office First Approach
Humans are wired for connection. Being office first is a core pillar of our culture because in-person connections drive your growth, learning, impact, and relationships. Strong relationships make it easier to disagree, give feedback, and do meaningful work together.
We're office first, not office only. Working from the office is our default, but we flex when needed. We have a high-trust culture where everyone is trusted to do what's best for Halter.
Our office vibe is special, the high energy and spectacular people make work enjoyable. Your growth and impact are unlimited here, coming from solving problems, innovating, and constantly learning from each other.
Join our team
Halter is committed to promoting a diverse and inclusive workplace — a place where we can each be ourselves and do the best work of our lives. Research shows that while men apply to jobs when they meet an average of 60% of the requirements, women and under-represented groups of candidates tend to only apply when they meet every requirement.

If you think you have what it takes but don’t necessarily tick every requirement on this job description, please still get in touch and apply to Halter. We’d love to chat to see if you’ll be an epic fit!

🎤 Why voize? Because we're more than just a job!
At voize, we believe the greatest gift to frontline workers is time - time to care, connect, and be present. Today, that time is lost to busywork and complex systems that pull them away from what matters most: people .
Our vision is to change that by building AI companions that seamlessly take over digital workflows. We don't replace humans with technology - we amplify their impact.
Our mission is backed with a $50M Series A funding led by Balderton Capital , with support from HV Capital, Y Combinator and other leading VCs. Today, 2,000+ facilities trust voize, and over 200,000 users rely on our AI companion to ease their daily workload.
As a dynamic team, we combine first-in-class technology with meaningful social impact. And now, we're looking for you to join us on this mission!

s.h: 💡 Your Mission: Turn growth into a system!
s.t:
Hi, I'm Jeremy, I lead RevOps at voize. I'm hiring the person who owns sales operations as we scale: new markets, new segments, and a sales team growing fast in all of them.
As Sales Operations Manager, you build the GTM engine that carries us past €100M ARR, working in close partnership with our sales leaders, with genuinely good tooling and AI ways of working behind you. Joining at this point in our hyper-growth journey is rare: big enough that the problems are real, early enough that you shape how they get solved. What you build now compounds for years, and so does your scope.
This role is roughly 60% building new process and 40% running what exists. If you want a mature machine to optimize, this is not it. If you want to design the machine, for now and for what comes next, it is.
🚀 Your Daily Business - No two days are alike
Territory, compensation & capacity. Own the global account, territory and book-of-business model. Carve books for new AEs, keep segmentation honest as we add hospitals and new geos, and build the capacity and quota model that underpins our fiscal plan.
Forecasting. Run the forecast process end to end with our VP Sales and team leads: weekly hygiene, submit and roll-up, quarterly commit. Diagnose why deals slip, and stand the process up in the US, France and UK as those teams ramp.
Insights the company acts on. Define the sales metrics we run on, then turn pipeline and funnel data into the analysis that steers board meetings, monthly GTM reviews and weekly deal inspection. You define what gets measured; our data and BI team build the layer underneath.
Commercial process. Design how non-standard deals are managed at voize. You set the rules and stand the function up; you will not be the approval queue.
Process and tool enablement. In close collaboration with sales enablement, you make sure what gets built actually gets adopted, partnering with leaders, AEs and SDRs to prioritize the work with the most impact.
The GTM stack, built AI-first. Own the sales side of CRM and the tools around it. Automate the manual layer with Claude, n8n and whatever else earns its place, and take a real position on which tooling we buy next as we scale.

s.h: 🤝 Your Skillset - What you bring to the table
s.t:
3+ years in revenue operations, sales operations or GTM strategy , at a fast-growing B2B SaaS company or in strategy/tech consulting, VC or M&A before an operating role. You have seen what breaks as a sales team scales, because you were the one who fixed it.
Exceptional stakeholder skills. You partner with VPs and team leads as an equal, push back with evidence, and get change adopted by people who do not report to you.
Sharp analytical instincts and deep CRM fluency. Expert in spreadsheets, comfortable reading data in a BI tool, and you have owned a HubSpot or Salesforce instance rather than just worked in one. You go deep on data enrichment and spot the patterns that keep our data model trustworthy.
You have supported forecasting. You can talk methodology, where it broke, and what you changed. Same for a territory or quota plan you built and aligned with sales leadership.
Entrepreneurial mindset and hands-on. You are comfortable with no playbook, you prioritize ruthlessly, and you ship rather than produce recommendations.
AI-native as a builder, not just a user. You already use Claude, n8n or similar to remove manual work from your own day, and you can point to something concrete you shipped that way.
🌱 Growing together - what you can expect at voize
We are a fast-growing startup, that means you will take on real problems, grow quickly, and make a real impact, giving frontline workers more time for people
We foster an open, collaborative culture with regular team events, whether you work from our Berlin office or remotely across Germany
Become a co-creator of our success with stock options
Generous perks: 30 vacation days plus your birthday off, Germany Transport Ticket, Urban Sports Club, regular company off-sites, and access to learning platforms such as Blinkist and Audible, plus free language courses
You decide when you work best, that means flexible working hours and a good hybrid set-up.
✨ Ready to talk? Apply now! 🚀
We look forward to your application and can't wait to meet you - no matter who you are or what background you have!

About 9fin
9fin is the AI platform powering global debt markets — the world’s largest asset class at over $145 trillion.
Debt markets are vast, global, and mission-critical, yet still run on fragmented data, PDFs, and manual workflows. 9fin replaces this broken infrastructure with a single platform that centralises proprietary credit data, deep analysis, and high-value workflows across global markets.
Today, 9fin powers teams at 300+ blue-chip institutions worldwide, including global banks, asset managers, private equity firms, law firms, and advisors. The business is scaling at exceptional speed, with rapid expansion in the US and best-in-class retention driven by deep workflow adoption.
We’re at a defining inflection point. With proven product-market fit and strong, global market pull, 9fin is accelerating toward becoming the category-defining platform for debt markets worldwide.
The opportunity
We're hiring our first dedicated legal operations team member to sit at the heart of 9fin's growing Legal Affairs function. This is a broad, hands-on role and a rare opportunity to shape how a scale-up in-house legal team runs from the inside out.
You'll own the operational engine of the team: our contract lifecycle platform (Ironclad, which is deeply embedded across sales, procurement and RevOps), our commercial playbook (and developing non-commercial playbooks), our tech stack (including AI implementation), our front-door (right now, ticketing is done in Linear), our knowledge management (currently spread across multiple systems), our reporting and KPIs, and the tracking and governance around outside counsel spend.
You'll also be a project manager and a hands-on partner to the General Counsel. That includes co-drafting monthly and quarterly business reviews, leading and coordinating cross-functional initiatives (for example M&A diligence coordination, trademark portfolio work, or regulatory readiness workstreams), and holding a high bar for organisation so nothing on a small, fast-moving team drops.
You'll report to the General Counsel and work alongside legal colleagues in London and New York. This is a London-based role and we typically expect the team to be in the office three days a week.
What you’ll work on
Below is the shape of the role, laid out as prioritised by Now, Next and Later so you can see the broad strokes of the path ahead - but by no means is this set in stone. Priorities will move as we learn what's most useful in practice and you’ll have a big hand in shaping this further.
Now
Tune legal intake - help us build out the “front door” for legal requests across the business.
Partner with Sales, Finance, InfoSec and Procurement to streamline deal-desk and approval processes
Support on knowledge management and internal policy administration. Consolidate knowledge, templates, and other information in a clean accessible structure.
Build our external legal spend tracker from scratch. Categorise spend, log invoices and quotes, match to matter, and produce a monthly view for the General Counsel.
Own KPI reporting improvements against our Ironclad-fed dashboards. Expand coverage into intake, spend, cycle times, and other operational metrics.
Own operational and reporting support across the Legal function, including responses to internal stakeholders including Finance, RevOps, and the People team.
Next
Get inside and own our tech stack and know it end-to-end - Ironclad, Linear, Google Workspace, Notion, and the AI tools we've adopted or are evaluating.
Build, maintain and roll out templates, playbooks and self-serve legal resources so the business can move quickly.
Own Ironclad workflow hygiene and adoption end-to-end. Work with the team to clean up metadata and archiving, tighten approvals and signatory workflows, and work with commercial counsel to roll out training across sales, procurement, RevOps and other frequent users.
Bring structure and visibility across the team. Keep track of open projects, drive follow-through, and make sure balls do not drop across a small team with a lot of surface area.
Maintain our sales contract playbook. Keep it current, propose updates as commercial patterns and RevOps feedback surface them, and make sure the team is actually using it.
Later
Partner with the General Counsel to produce meaningful Exec-level reporting.
Assist with management of large legal projects on GC instruction. Recent examples include M&A diligence coordination, and trademark portfolio work.
Support company secretarial administration.

We're looking for a highly organised operator who is energised by building order out of scale-up complexity. You do not need to be a lawyer, but you do need to have run legal operations end-to-end before. The essentials come first below, followed by preferred experience and the traits we care about most.
Highly organised with a systems mindset: You keep the plates spinning and notice when one wobbles. You see the workflow behind the task and design for repeatability.
Commercial, action-biased, comfortable with ambiguity: You understand what the business needs from legal, get things over the line without waiting to be asked twice, and you're comfortable being the first hire writing the map as you go.
Ironclad or equivalent CLM: Hands-on experience with Ironclad or a directly comparable enterprise CLM (for example Juro, LinkSquares, Icertis, Agiloft, Leah). We are deeply embedded in Ironclad and you will own it.
Legal operations track record: At least five years' experience running legal operations, contracts operations or a closely adjacent function (compliance operations, legal project management, or legal chief-of-staff), ideally in a scale-up or in-house legal team that is fast paced and where you can demonstrate ownership.
End-to-end project delivery: You have owned legal or cross-functional projects on your own steam, including timelines, risks, stakeholders and outcomes.
Reporting and data fluency: You can build clean dashboards, work with a KPI framework, and translate metrics into a story someone can act on.
Outside counsel spend or panel exposure: Experience setting up spend tracking, panel management or legal project management would be useful, but we're also open to someone with the capability and appetite to build this from scratch.
Builder mentality: Experience as a team’s first or only legal-ops hire, or a member of a small team in the early stage of the build-out of a legal ops function, would be a strong advantage.

We’re a scaling start up, and we enjoy sharing our success, when the company succeeds, we always reinvest that in our people. We also offer huge amounts of responsibility, an abundance of opportunity for growth and a platform to truly excel.

Job Summary : The Content Review Operations Coordinator is responsible for managing and executing the end-to-end medical, legal, and regulatory review processes for promotional or medical content within Genentech.

Unser Kunde ist ein junges Reinigungsunternehmen in der Region Basel. Das Unternehmen wurde vor rund zwei Jahren gegründet und beschäftigt aktuell rund vier Mitarbeitende. Die Eigentümer haben die Firma bisher neben ihren bestehenden Unternehmen aufgebaut und geführt. Aufgrund des Wachstums möchte man die operative Verantwortung nun schrittweise an eine engagierte Führungspersönlichkeit übergeben.

Es handelt sich um eine junge, noch nicht perfekt strukturierte Firma, die mit dieser Stelle bewusst in Vorleistung geht. In den ersten Monaten liegt der Fokus stark auf operativer Mitarbeit – Sie reinigen mit, während gemeinsam die Strukturen aufgebaut werden.

Sie arbeiten sehr selbständig, mit wenig enger Führung – eine wöchentliche operative Sitzung, sonst vieles ad hoc. Erwartet wird, dass Sie aktiv auf Kunden zugehen und selbst Aufträge akquirieren; dafür werden Sie direkt am Erfolg beteiligt. Kurz gesagt: eine Rolle mit viel
Eigenverantwortung, die unternehmerisches Denken und Eigeninitiative wirklich braucht.

* Aktive Mitarbeit vor Ort, insbesondere in der Anfangsphase – Sie sind sich nicht zu schade, selbst mit anzupacken
* Führung, Betreuung und Einsatzplanung der Mitarbeitenden
* Organisation, Koordination und Kontrolle der laufenden Reinigungsaufträge
* Sicherstellung einer hohen Arbeitsqualität und Kundenzufriedenheit
* Betreuung bestehender Kunden sowie Bearbeitung von Reklamationen und Anliegen

* Optimierung und Weiterentwicklung interner Abläufe und Prozesse
* Enge, aber wenig kleinteilige Zusammenarbeit mit den Eigentümern (u.a. eine wöchentliche operative Sitzung)

* Erfahrung in der Reinigungsbranche ist ein Plus, aber keine Voraussetzung – Einarbeitung erfolgt

The General Manager, Financial Services Risk & Compliance Operations, is a senior leadership role responsible for building and leading Xero’s line 1 financial services risk and compliance operations capability, and will be one of the Responsible Managers for Australian Financial Services Licensing purposes.
This role establishes the operating function that enables Xero to scale regulated financial services safely and confidently. It brings together sanctions screening, KYB/KYC and identity verification, AML/CTF operational execution, transaction monitoring, and payment operations into a single, high-performing function that protects customer trust while supporting product growth.
The GM will lead the function through its build-operate-transfer phase, initially within Advocacy, Risk & Compliance and, once stable and mature, into its permanent line 1 home. The role will set direction, build the team, define operating standards, and create the partnerships needed across Product, Payments, CX, Security, Financial Services Legal, Risk & Compliance and Enterprise Risk & Compliance to ensure Xero is regulator-ready and operationally strong.
This role is critical to ensuring Xero can take direct ownership of the customer and regulatory obligations that come with expanding payments and other financial services products. It represents an opportunity to build trusted operational infrastructure that enables growth, strengthens resilience, and supports a seamless customer experience.
What You’ll Focus On
Setting up core operational capabilities across sanctions screening, KYB/KYC verification, AML/CTF execution, and payment workflows.
Tooling optimization across Sardine, Salesforce workflows, payment operations platforms, and third-party payment portals.
Establishing operational governance routines, service standards, and key escalation pathways like the Financial Crime and Fraud Working Group.
Managing relationships and quality oversight for outsourced operational partners to align with internal control expectations.

Substantial operational leadership background within financial crime, AML/CTF, payment operations, or regulated financial services.
Proven capability in building or scaling first-line risk functions, establishing operational controls, and guiding teams through organizational growth.
Deep practical understanding of sanctions, KYB/KYC, transaction monitoring, and financial services licensing frameworks.
Skill in managing external partner relationships, service quality standards, and operational service level agreements.
Comfort using operational data, trend analysis, and workflow tools to continuously strengthen controls and improve efficiency.
Confidence utilizing AI tools responsibly to aid operational decision-making, manage data risks, and streamline team workflows.
Apply even if your experience isn't a perfect match! At Xero, we hire based on your skills, passion, and the unique perspective you can bring to enhance our culture and team.
Where and how you can work
This position offers a flexible hybrid working model, balancing the autonomy of remote work with purposeful, collaborative time spent in our modern office spaces. You will participate in regular boost days designed to bring teams together for strategic alignment, creative brainstorming, and connection. Specific location arrangements and remote options can be discussed based on your region.

The Associate General Manager, Dealership Operations is responsible for the success of the dealership’s service & parts businesses, overall facilities management, and OEM relationship. What you’ll be doing
Management – Service & Parts Operations
Lead all aspects of the dealership’s Service and Parts operations to achieve revenue, gross profit, and customer satisfaction targets.
Oversee daily/weekly performance reviews, analyzing KPIs (CSI, RO count, gross profit, efficiency) and implementing action plans to hit targets.

Partner with Service and Parts Managers to improve workflow, reduce cycle times, and maximize shop and parts department throughput.
Monitor warranty processes to ensure compliance and maximize claim recovery.
Continuously improve customer experience, speed of service, and first-time fix rate.

Enforce workplace safety standards, OSHA requirements, and loss-prevention measures to protect associates and customers.
Relationship – OEM & Brand Alignment
Serve as primary liaison with OEM representatives across service, parts, and facility compliance.
Ensure alignment with OEM warranty policies, recall processes, and customer satisfaction programs.
Proactively manage OEM facility inspections, responding to audit findings and driving timely resolution of issues.
Represent Carvana in OEM meetings and performance reviews, consistently achieving or exceeding manufacturer objectives.
Build and sustain positive working relationships with OEM field teams to ensure strong collaboration and support.
People Leadership & Development
Recruit, hire, and retain high-performing Service and Parts teams; maintain a bench of candidates for key leadership positions.
Establish and oversee training, certification, and career progression programs for associates at all levels.
Deliver competency-based feedback and performance reviews to drive accountability and growth.
Mentor Service and Parts Managers to strengthen leadership capabilities and operational execution.
Foster a culture of teamwork, engagement, and continuous improvement throughout the dealership.
Continuous Improvement
Identify and prioritize opportunities for process and performance improvement across fixed operations.
Lead and sponsor Lean/Kaizen initiatives that increase efficiency, reduce costs, and enhance customer experience.
Hold teams accountable for measurable results from continuous improvement efforts.

Lead the operational delivery of internal Remote Operations and Feature Testing activities.
Translate testing priorities and business requirements into clear tactical plans for the VSO team.
Plan and coordinate testing activities across different locations and countries where required.
Work closely with internal stakeholders to align on testing priorities, operational feasibility and delivery plans.
Support the prioritisation of testing activities based on business needs, staffing, vehicle readiness, safety requirements, local constraints and delivery risks.
Ensure daily testing activities are delivered safely, efficiently and in line with agreed KPIs, testing goals and operational standards.
Balance vehicle availability, staffing, shift coverage and testing requirements to maximise productive testing time.
Identify operational blockers early and work with the relevant teams to resolve them.
Ensure the team is prepared for new testing requirements, feature testing activities, remote support missions and changes in operational scope.
Line manage the Remote Operations and Feature Testing VSOs, supporting performance, development, engagement and wellbeing.
Lead team performance management by setting clear expectations, supporting development and ensuring concerns are addressed consistently and professionally.
Ensure new processes, SOPs and operational changes are communicated clearly and applied consistently across the team.
Act as escalation point for safety concerns, operational risks and serious incidents.
Promote a safety-first culture where concerns are raised early and acted on appropriately.
Use data, operational feedback and team input to improve planning, utilisation, issue resolution and testing delivery.
Support the scaling of internal testing operations while maintaining safety, quality and consistency.

Essential
Proven experience in operational management, ideally in automotive testing, fleet operations, logistics, technology operations or another fast-paced operational environment.
Strong people leadership experience, including direct management of operational teams.
Ability to translate high-level priorities into clear operational plans.
Strong understanding of resource planning, shift planning and performance management.
Experience managing operational KPIs, identifying performance gaps and driving improvements.
Strong communication skills and confidence working with cross-functional stakeholders.
Ability to make sound decisions under pressure and manage competing priorities.
Strong safety mindset and experience operating in a controlled or safety-sensitive environment.
Comfortable working in a dynamic environment where plans can change quickly.
Ability to work across teams and influence priorities by providing clear operational input.
Desirable
Experience with ADAS, autonomous vehicle testing, automotive development or remote operations.
Understanding of vehicle testing, data collection, feature testing or safety driver operations.
Experience working with VSOs, technicians, field engineers or similar operational teams.
Experience planning operational activities across different countries or markets.
German language skills or experience working within German operational environments.

The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries.

It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for.

s.h: About the Role, Mission or Department Overview
s.t:
Wirecutter is seeking a photo editor and operations coordinator to keep our Store- and editorial-focused photo pipeline running smoothly. You will ensure that photographers can focus on shooting and craft while our workflows, logistics, and day-to-day editing are handled with care and consistency.
In this role, you'll manage the operational side of our photography with an emphasis on the Store: scheduling, asset flow, file management, and repeatable workflows. You'll also serve as a photo editor for the Store and other editorial projects. You'll act as creative connective tissue across editorial, marketing, commerce, and product, making sure Store photo needs and timelines are aligned across teams and that visuals reflect Wirecutter's standards.
You'll work from our Long Island City studio and collaborate closely with Wirecutter's photo team, editors, designers, audience and marketing partners, and product colleagues.
This role is based in New York City and will require regular in-person work in our studio.

s.h: Coordinate logistics for Store and editorial shoots
s.t:
Schedule Store and editorial shoots, manage calendars, and ensure photographers have the time and information they need to execute.
Book freelance stylists, models, and other collaborators as needed, in partnership with creative leadership and operations.
Manage studio time and resources so Store and editorial priorities are balanced and predictable.
Serve as photo editor for the Wirecutter Store and key editorial packages:
Partner with editors and designers to select images, shape visual narratives, and maintain quality and consistency across Store PDPs, collections, and editorial features.
Apply and help uphold Wirecutter's visual standards, making sure Store imagery reflects our reporting, testing, and brand voice.
Provide clear feedback and guidance to photographers and collaborators on selects, crops, and retouching.

s.h: Own day-to-day post-production and asset management
s.t:
Handle basic post-production for Store and editorial imagery, including editing, color, and light retouching.
Ingest, organize, and file images so assets are tagged, searchable, and easy to reuse across Store, editorial, and off-platform surfaces.
Manage asset delivery for cross-functional partners, ensuring the right files reach the right teams.

s.h: Partner with marketing, commerce, and product on asset needs
s.t:
Work with marketing and commerce teams to understand campaign timelines, asset needs, and how Store visuals will be used across channels Align photo production plans with Store and editorial calendars so key moments have the visuals they need.
Serve as a clear point of contact for Store-related photo questions.

s.h: Help codify and scale repeatable workflows
s.t:
Document cross-team workflows (from brief to shoot to deployment) so non-editorial partners understand how to request, use, and find Store visuals.
Create and maintain checklists, templates, and process documentation that make Store shoots more predictable and efficient.
Identify bottlenecks in our photo operations and propose improvements that free up photographers to spend more time on creative work.
Perform related work as assigned.
Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.
You will report to the Creative Director, NYT Wirecutter.

3–5 years of experience in photo editing, photo operations, or a related visuals role within an editorial, ecommerce, or media environment.
Demonstrated experience coordinating shoots, managing photo workflows, or supporting a studio or visuals team.
Photo-editing skills and an eye for visual storytelling, including experience selecting, sequencing, and refining images to support clear narratives and consistent standards.
Proficiency with Photoshop, along with familiarity with asset management and file organization best practices.

Comfort working with multiple stakeholders and balancing competing priorities, with project-management and organizational skills.
3+ years of experience collaborating with cross-functional partners, such as editors, designers, marketing, commerce, and product teams. As well as an ability to communicate clearly and diplomatically across those groups.
Familiarity with studio operations, including scheduling, basic equipment knowledge, and working with photographers and stylists.
A deep interest in Wirecutter's mission and a commitment to upholding our standards for independence, rigor, and service journalism in all Store and editorial visuals.
This position is represented by the NewsGuild of NY.
